reasoning_traces.think:
The P3 primitive formalizes penetrative passing as a geometric problem involving convex hulls of opponent formations. It defines a pass as 'potential' if a teammate can receive within the convex hull formed by opponents in front of the ball. This is modeled mathematically as a set membership condition: $\mathcal{P}_3 = \{ p \in \mathbb{R}^2 \mid \exists T \subset \text{Opponents} \text{ s.t. } \text{conv}(T) \ni p \}$, where $p$ is the pass location and $T$ is the set of opponent positions. The binary classifier $f(X)$ maps pre-event features to a probability of success, with AUC ROC as the primary metric due to class imbalance. The convex hull feasibility kernel $\mathcal{F}(p, T)$ evaluates whether a pass is geometrically viable. These primitives form a dual structure: one for defining potential (geometric), another for predicting realization (statistical). Failure modes include data leakage from post-event features, camera bias affecting hull computation, and overfitting in ML models. The system's robustness depends on accurate opponent positioning and feature engineering.
